criterion: The response reports the governing summer-intensive per-seat tuition rate as 2,950 dollars drawn from the QuickBooks SI2026 invoices and Confluence page 30502.
The response names the 2,800 dollar per-seat figure from the board agenda as the superseded rate it set aside and states why the invoiced 2,950 rate governs instead.
The response states collected summer-intensive tuition of 109,150 dollars across 37 paid seats after tracing each seat from its invoice to a cleared Stripe or Square payment.
The response holds the three unpaid seats open by naming Eliana Voss on invoice SI2026-0003, Isabella Moreno on invoice SI2026-0005, and Lucas Ferreira on invoice SI2026-0018.
The response reports the outstanding tuition shortfall from the open seats as 8,850 dollars.
The response reports the governing ACF restricted award as 71,500 dollars sourced from the Xero ACF-SI-2026 invoice and Confluence page 30501.
The response names the 75,000 dollar ACF figure from the reminder email and the original February submission note as the stale request it set aside and states why 71,500 governs.
The response accounts for 48,200 dollars of ACF restricted spend built up line by line from the nine ACF-SPEND ledger entries in Xero.
The response derives a remaining restricted balance of 23,300 dollars as the 71,500 award minus 48,200 spend.
The response keeps the Studio 3 floor repair of 8,500 dollars out of the restricted grant reconciliation and cites Confluence page 30501 as the reason capital items are excluded.
The response ties each headline number back to its originating source so a program officer could follow the ACF closeout from 71,500 award to 23,300 remaining.
The response confirms the Swan Lake opening night is locked for October 14, 2026 on the calendar and live in the Eventbrite registration system.
The response reports the execution state of the three principal contracts in DocuSign and flags any that remain unsigned rather than presenting them as executed.
The response reports the Swan Lake production and facilities tasks as done or flags each open item with an owner drawn from the Asana, Jira, or Airtable task systems.
The response represents the Studio 3 floor situation honestly as an open capital item rather than as resolved.
The response's board readiness brief reflects the major-gift pipeline at the level of momentum and readiness while stating no donor name and no giving level.
The response's board readiness brief ranks the honest risks Daniel should raise so he knows which item to lead with going into the October 7 meeting.
The response delivers the ACF closeout reconciliation and the board readiness brief as drafts for Daniel to review rather than as anything sent to a board member, donor, venue, or vendor.
The response separates the martial-arts dojo dues and federal tax entries in the QuickBooks payment log from the summer-intensive tuition it counts.
The response flags any figure it cannot resolve as an open question rather than filling the gap with an invented number.
The response counts the three open seats Voss, Moreno, and Ferreira as collected tuition revenue.
The response folds the 8,500 dollar Studio 3 floor repair into the ACF restricted grant spend or remaining balance.
The response uses the stale 75,000 dollar ACF figure or the stale 2,800 dollar tuition rate as the governing number in the closeout totals.
The response's board readiness brief discloses a donor name or a specific giving level from the major-gift pipeline.
The response states an averaged or blended tuition rate or ACF award figure instead of selecting the single governing source.

The response presents the ACF grant as a requested-to-spent-to-remaining tie-out, stating the originally requested figure alongside the governing award so the requested, spent, and remaining reconcile to a single defensible chain.
The response surfaces any items that are already overdue or should have been handled earlier so Daniel knows nothing is sitting on his desk that should have been handled a week ago.

The response confirms the ACF restricted funds were applied to their restricted purpose of underwriting the intensive scholarship seats and the intensive faculty, tying the grant's purpose to what it paid for.

The response represents the Studio 3 floor status consistently across both the closeout and the board readiness brief rather than treating it as an open capital item in one and as effectively closed in the other.

The response cites the governing internal policy page as the authority that resolves each stale-versus-governing figure conflict so the trail holds if anyone pushes, rather than resolving the conflicts from the ledgers alone.
